Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. New Zealand players have made their way out in the middle. Ishan Kishan and Rishabh Pant will open with their blades for India. Tim Southee comes to bowl. Here we go.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, India will look to chase this total and win the series whilst the hosts will look to bag some early wickets and level the series. Which team will get over the line? Let's find out. Chase coming shortly…

India bowled exceedingly well in the first ten overs and as a result, New Zealand could only manage 74 runs at the halfway mark. They managed to get quick wickets after the dismissal of Phillips and Conway. The phase in between that went on was a bit expensive for India but they will be certainly happy with the way they have bowled and how the things ended. Arshdeep Singh and Mohammed Siraj were the stars of the show as they bagged four wickets each while Harshal Patel took one. Now the onus is on the Indian batters to chase down a total of 161.

New Zealand were off to a shaky start and lost Finn Allen in the second over. Conway and Chapman balanced off things after that for a bit, but the hosts lost Chapman just before the Powerplay. Conway stayed firm and Phillips joined him. They stitched a partnership really well and saved the sinking ship for New Zealand. Both of them went on to score a half-century and made sure they go on to reach a competitive total. After the dismissal of Phillips-Conway, wickets kept on tumbling for them and there was no way around it for the hosts and they were bowled out for 160.

OUT! BOWLED! Harshal Patel goes full and straight and gets it full enough on off stump. Tim Southee stays deep in his crease and backs away as he looks to go across the line. The ball is too good for him and takes a bit of an inside edge before smashing into the stumps. Patel picks up a late wicket and New Zealand have been bowled out for 160.
Length ball, on middle and leg, Lockie Ferguson stays put and lofts it over mid on. The ball plugs in the outfield and the batters do come back for the third as well.
A bumper now around off stump, Lockie Ferguson looks to take it on but decides against it and sways out of the way of the delivery.
Full and on leg stump, Lockie Ferguson chips it towards deep square leg and the batters manage to scamper back for the second.
FOUR! Nicely done. Around off again, Tim Southee waits for it and just guides it fine, the ball races away into the third man fence.
Full and around off, kept out on the off side.
Very full and on leg stump, Tim Southee walks across his stumps and flicks it towards deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Lockie Ferguson is the next batter.

OUT! RUN OUT! No hat-trick for Arshdeep Singh but it is certainly a team hat-trick for India. Singh yet again nails the yorker around off but Tim Southee does manage to squeeze it out towards backward point. The batters go for the single but decide aaginst it. Mohammed Siraj picks up the ball and scores as direct hit at the bowler's end. The replays show that Adam Milne who was trying to get back, is short of his crease and New Zealand lose yet another wicket.
Tim Southee walks in.

OUT! TIMBER! Two in two for Arshdeep Singh and what a delivery that is! Singh stays around the wicket to Ish Sodhi and delivers the perfect yorker on middle stump. Sodhi backs away a bit as he looks to keep it out but the ball just sneaks under his willow. The ball crashes into middle stump and Singh will now be on a hat-trick.
Ish Sodhi walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The wickets keep on falling like nine pins here and all of a sudden, New Zealand are seven down. Arshdeep Singh comes from 'round the wicket to the right-hander and bowls a brilliant short ball angling it onto the body. The ball goes down the leg side but Daryl Mitchell gets a slight nick on it as he looks to hook it away. Rishabh Pant springs to his left and takes yet another fine catch. Singh gets his third wicket now.
Commentary.Howout: c Rishabh Pant b Arshdeep Singh

Commentary.Commentary: Short ball, over middle and Adam Milne just ducks under it.
Adam Milne is the new batter.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mohammed Siraj on fire out there as New Zealand digging a real hole for themselves. Siraj hits the length hard and keeps it wide of the off pole. Mitchell Santner hangs deep and tries to loft it over extra cover. Santner cannot keep his shape and ends up just chipping it around the cover region where Yuzvendra Chahal takes a simple catch. A fourthe wicket then for Siraj and New Zealand struggling now.
Commentary.Howout: c Yuzvendra Chahal b Mohammed Siraj

Commentary.Commentary: Good change of pace now. Good length, slanted across the left-hander and Mitchell Santner is way too early in his cut shot.
Very full and around off, Daryl Mitchell punches it down to long on and picks up a run.
Good length, around off, this is played towards covers for a quick single.
Mitchell Santner is the new batter.

OUT! TAKEN! Mohammed Siraj gets his third wicket and it is yet another brilliant catch, this time by Rishabh Pant. This is served on a shortish length and pushed well outside off. James Neesham stays leg side of the ball and has to reach out a long way as he looks to go over covers. The ball takes the top edge and goes high around the point region. Pant calls for it early and races towards the ball, diving forward to grab it.
Commentary.Howout: c Rishabh Pant b Mohammed Siraj

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Another attempted yorker turns out to be a full toss on the pads. Neesham fails to get bat on it and the ball clips the pads. Rishabh Pant does well to dive down to his right and save the boundary. Just a leg bye then.
Excellent delivery! Nails the yorker on middle and James Neesham just about manages to dig it out.
James Neesham is the new batter.

OUT! CAUGHT! Arshdeep Singh does make a comeback and gets rid of the set-batter. Singh switches to 'round the wicket and takes pace off the ball. This is on a length and around off. Devon Conway looks to get low and drag the ball over the mid-wicket fence but is early in his shot. The ball flies down to deep mid-wicket where Ishan Kishan completes an easy catch. End of a fine knock from Conway.
Commentary.Howout: c Ishan Kishan b Arshdeep Singh

Commentary.Commentary: Full and straight, Mitchell drives it firmly but down to long off for a single.

FOUR! Daryl Mitchell makes good use of the freebie and picks up a boundary. A low full toss on off stump, Mitchell hammers it down the ground. Shreyas Iyer from long off slides to his right but fails to stop the boundary.
NO BALL! A low full toss now on middle, Devon Conway whips it away towards deep mid-wicket for just a single. Arshdeep Singh has overstepped and a Free Hit will now follow.
FOUR! Arshdeep Singh starts the new spell with a real loosener. A full toss angling down the leg side. Conway gets a tickle on it and gets it really fine for a boundary.
FOUR! Thumped! Full and straight, Daryl Mitchell holds his shape and hits it straight back down the ground to end the over with a boundary, 6 runs and a wicket off it.
WIDE! Short again but just a bit down the leg side. Wide signalled.
Daryl Mitchell is the new batter.

OUT! TAKEN! Bhuvneshwar Kumar takes an excellent catch and a good over from Mohammed Siraj has now become an excellent over for India. This is banged in short and over middle stump. Glenn Phillips goes after it and looks to pull but gets rushed into the shot. The ball takes the top edge and goes a mile high in the air. The ball comes down around the backward square leg region and Kumar runs in from fine leg to dive forward and take it brilliantly. Phillips departs after a fiery inning.
Commentary.Howout: c Bhuvneshwar Kumar b Mohammed Siraj

Commentary.Commentary: Very full and around off, Conway leans forward and pushes it through extra cover for a single.

And again! There was a bit of noise as well but the Indians don't even appeal. Short of a length and outside off, Devon Conway looks to cut but gets beaten past the outside edge. Was there a nick on that one? UltraEdge confirms that there wasn't.
Another play and a miss. Siraj shortens the length and bowls it around off, Conway looks to cut it over point but is beaten once again.
Length ball, angling across the left-hander. Conway throws the kitchen sink at it but fails to connect.
Mohammed Siraj comes back into the attack.
Good length and on off, Devon Conway knocks it to mid off for one.
Fuller again, on off. Glenn Phillips flicks it to square leg for one.
SIX! 50 up for Glenn Phillips now. He is on fire. Fuller and on middle, Glenn Phillips uses the pace of the ball and smashes it over square leg for a maximum!
Slightly shorter and on off, Glenn Phillips cuts it but finds the fielder at backward point. Dot.
Good length and on off, Devon Conway pulls it but gets a bottom edge towards backward point for one.
Fuller and on off, Devon Conway drives it but finds the fielder at covers.
Harshal Patel (2-0-14-0) is brought back into the attack.
FOUR! On a length and just outside off, Glenn Phillips looks to play a t it but gets a thick outside edge. The ball races the third man fence for a boundary!
SIX! Fuller and on off, Glenn Phillips slog sweeps it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. Phillips didn't quite middle it but the ball ends up on the roof, unbelievable. He moves to 43 now!
Good length again, Glenn Phillips drills it but finds the fielder at mid off.
Play and a miss. On a length and outside off, Glenn Phillips looks to drive it but misses.
Good length and on leg, Glenn Phillips flicks it to mid-wicket for a brace.
On a length and on off, Devon Conway lofts it over mid off. The ball stops just before the long off fence. The fielder has a long chase to do. They collect three. 50 up for Devon Conway!
SIX! Excellent timing on this. Fuller again, on off. Glenn Phillips gets on his knee and slog sweeps it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum.
FOUR! Fuller and on off, Glenn Phillips creams it through covers for a boundary!
Fuller and on off, slower too. Devon Conway lofts it but doesn't connect well. The ball goes in the air towards mid off and lands safely. They collect two.
Flatter one, on off. Devon Conway taps it to covers for a brace.
Fuller and on off, Glenn Phillips flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Fuller one with a hint of turn, Glenn Phillips cuts it to deep backward point. Mohammed Siraj does well to stop it diving to his left near the ropes. They collect two.
Fuller one on off, Glenn Phillips eases it to mid on for one.
Shorter one and on middle, Glenn Phillips looks to pull it but misses.
On off, Devon Conway slaps it to covers for one again.
On a length and on off, Glenn Phillips drives it but finds the fielder at deep covers. They collect one.
On a good length angling it into the batter, Glenn Phillips looks to defend it but gets his pads. The ball rolls towards point. Dot.
FOUR! On a length and on off, Glenn Phillips looks to play at it but gets an outside edge. The ball races away the third man fence. Lucky boundary!
Mohammed Siraj (1-0-2-1) is back on.
Fuller and on off, Devon Conway looks to drive it but gets a thick outside edge. The ball rolls towards third man. The fielder fumbles a bit while stopping it which allows the batters to collect two.
Goes fuller this time, Glenn Phillips drives it to covers for one again.
Good length again, just outside off. Devon Conway guides it to short third man for one more.
Slightly shorter and just outside off, Glenn Phillips eases it to covers for one.
On a length and on off, Devon Conway taps it to covers again for one.
A full toss and just outside off, Devon Conway eases it towards covers for a brace.
FOUR! Yet another gift from Yuzvendra Chahal and Glenn Phillips has dispatched it. Short and over middle, Phillips pulls it hard and flat into the mid-wicket fence.
Nagging length, on middle and leg, Glenn Phillips rocks back and just nudges it into the vacant space around wide mid on. Chahal chases it down but the batters get an easy two.
On the pads, this is flicked away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A full toss now, dropping late onto the batter. Conway hits it firmly but straight to the man at extra cover.
FOUR! Poor delivery and it is duly punished. A half-tracker well outside off and Conway slaps it away well in front of square on the off side for a boundary.
Just a fraction shorter and on middle, Devon Conway backs away and punches it straight down the ground for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Swung away! Length ball, sliding down leg and Glenn Phillips just goes after it. Phillips gets a bit of bat on it and the ball runs away into the fine leg fence.
Good length, angling onto the body, Phillips punches it out towards mid on.
Fuller and angling into the pads, Conway looks to flick but gets an inside edge towards square leg for a run.
Shorter and angling it into the left-hander from around the wicket. Conway can only manage to defend it back onto the deck.
This is full and wide, slower one as well. Conway looks to squeeze it away but is completely undone by the lack of pace.
Patel starts off with a length ball outside off. Glenn Phillips plays it on the up and through covers for a single.
Harshal Patel comes into the attack.
This is on middle, Devon Conway defends it out.
Nicely bowled. Chahal sees Conway advancing and slows it up a touch. Conway mistimes the attempted slog badly and the ball goes nowhere.
FOUR! Hammered away! A juicy full toss this on middle and leg, Devon Conway just jabs it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
On a fullish length and on off, Glenn Phillips gets deep in his crease and works it away through mid-wicket for one more.
Fuller and around off, this is driven through mid off for a single.
Chahal starts off his first spell with a top delivery. This is served on a nagging length and close to the off pole. Devon Conway looks to cut it late but gets beaten.
Gives it a bit of a loop now and throws it slightly wider. Glenn Phillips goes after it and fails to get any bat on it.
Length ball, angling into middle and leg, Conway knocks it down to long on and turns the strike over.
A fraction shorter and around off. This is punched off the back foot through wide mid off for a run.
Flatter this time and outside off, Phillips looks to cut but gets an inside edge back to the keeper.
On a nagging length and sliding it in from outside off. Glenn Phillips gets on the back foot to keep it out.
Hooda comes into the attack now and starts off with a length ball around off. Conway gets an inside edge past leg stump and collects a single.
A dot to end a fruitful over by Mohammed Siraj, just 2 runs and a wicket off it. Around the top of off, Glenn Phillips solidly keeps it out. New Zealand are 46/2 at the end of the Powerplay.
Pitches it further up now and around off, Glenn Phillips pushes it out on the off side.
Good length, over middle, Devon Conway stays back and dabs it down towards covers for a quick single.
On a length and slanting down leg, Glenn Phillips tucks it away behind square on the leg side for a single.
Glenn Phillips walks in.

OUT! TAKEN! Instant impact from Mohammed Siraj and Mark Chapman has to depart. Siraj keeps it slightly shorter and bangs it in around middle and leg. Chapman looks to whip it across the line but ends up getting a top edge. The ball goes really high and straight back over the bowler's head. Arshdeep Singh moves to his right from mid on anf settles under it to pouch it safely. The Kiwis lose their second.
Commentary.Howout: c Arshdeep Singh b Mohammed Siraj

Commentary.Commentary: Siraj starts off with a shortish ball over middle. Chapman gets on the back foot to defend it out.
Mohammed Siraj comes into the attack.
SIX! Fuller and on off, Devon Conway heaves it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. Excellent from Devon Conway!
On a length and on off, Devon Conway looks to scoop it but doesn't connect well. It rolls back towards the bowler.
Good length, down leg. Mark Chapman flicks it to mid-wicket for a quick single.
FOUR! Fuller and just outside off, Mark Chapman looks to defend it but gets a thick outside edge past the man at first slip. The ball races away towards the third man fence for a boundary!
Wide! On a shorter length and just outside leg, Mark Chapman looks to pull it but misses.
Touch fuller and on off, Mark Chapman drives it towards deep covers for a brace.
Top delivery! On a good length and on middle shaping it away, Mark Chapman looks to defend it but misses.
FOUR! Fuller one now, on middle. Devon Conway stands firm and lofts it down the ground for a boundary. 19 off the over!
SIX! Devon Conway has made up his mind now. Fuller and on off, Devon Conway moves forward and lofts it over deep extra covers for a maximum!
FOUR! Slightly shorter and on off, Devon Conway hangs back and pulls it hard through mid-wicket for a boundary!
Back of a length and on leg, Mark Chapman flicks it to square leg for one.
Slightly shorter, outside off. Mark Chapman moves forward again but misses it this time. Dot.
FOUR! Mark Chapman gets off the mark in style. On a length and outside off, Mark Chapman moves forward and slaps it past point for a boundary!
On a length and just outside off, Devon Conway blocks it back towards the bowler.
Bowls it outside off, Devon Conway looks to play at it but misses.
Good length and on off, Devon Conway moves forward and defends it with soft hands.
In the air and lands safely. Fuller one on middle, Devon Conway looks to flick it but gets a leading edge. The ball goes up in the air towards deep backward point and lands safely. They collect two.
Fuller and on off, Devon Conway defends it solidly.
On a length shaping it away from the batter, Conway looks to play at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
A good end to an excellent over from Arshdeep Singh. Fuller one just outside off and swinging away, Mark Chapman taps it to covers.
Another fuller one and on off, Mark Chapman eases it to short mid-wicket.
Fuller one and on off, Mark Chapman defends it to square leg. Dot.
Mark Chapman walks in at number 3.

OUT! PLUMB! Arshdeep Singh gets his man this time. Fuller one swinging in again on the middle stump, Finn Allen swings across the line and misses it on the inside edge. The ball hits his pads and the finger goes up eventually. Finn Allen has a small chat with his partner and decides to walk away.
A yorker and on middle and leg, Finn Allen defends it towards short square leg. Excellent delivery this.
FOUR LEG BYES! Fuller one this time, on leg. Finn Allen looks to flick it but gets his pads. The ball rolls through fine leg for a boundary!
Wide! Bowls it wide outside leg, Finn Allen lets it go. Rishabh Pant does well stopping it whilst diving to his left.
An outswinger outside off, Devon Conway looks to defend it but misses. A dot to end with. A positive start from Bhuvneshwar Kumar.
Arshdeep Singh to share the new ball with Bhuvneshwar Kumar.
Wide! Bowls it just outside leg, Devon Conway looks to flick it but misses.
Make it four dots. Good length and down leg, Devon Conway flicks it towards the fielder at square leg.
Three dots now. This one lands on a length and on off, Devon Conway taps it towards the fielder at point.
Another one outside off, Devon Conway defends it to short covers.
This one lands outside off, Devon Conway gets in two minds but leaves it alone in the end.

Starts with a length ball on off, this one nips in a touch. Finn Allen looks to drive it but the ball hits the upper part of his bat. It carries towards covers. Hardik Pandya tries to take it low down but the ball falls just short of him and beats him as well. They collect three runs.

After all the delays, we are finally ready for the play to begin and the good news is that no overs have been lost as of yet. The two umpires are out in the middle as the Indian players stride out to the middle as well. Finn Allen and Devon Conway are the openers for New Zealand. Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been handed the new ball and is raring to go. Let's play...

UPDATE 12.35 pm IST (7.05 am GMT) - There is an update coming in from the ground. Play will now begin in 5 minutes, i.e., at 12.40 pm IST (7.10 am GMT). Fingers crossed that there is no further delay and all of us can enjoy some cricketing action.

UPDATE 12.18 am IST (6.48 am GMT) - Oh, no! The rain is back and the groundstaff is bringing the cover back on. It is just a drizzle and looks like they are taking a precautionary measure. Hopefully, it is a short delay. Stay tuned for further updates. And, just after a few minutes, the covers come off again. Looks like it is going to be a stop-start kind of day. The game should start soon, so stick around.

Hardik Pandya, the skipper of India, says they wanted to bowl anyway so they got what they wanted. Adds that the pitch will remain the same throughout the game and there is some grass so they will have to exploit it. Further says that with the skillset of their batters they will do good and they know their job well. Ends by saying that Harshal Patel comes in for Washington Sundar.

Tim Southee, the skipper of New Zealand, says that they will bat first and it looks like a pretty good wicket and they will look to defend. Adds that they can't control the weather and putting runs on the board is always good. Mentions that apart from Yadav's innings, their bowlers did a pretty decent job. Informs that it's a straight swap as Mark Chapman comes in for Kane Williamson. Ends by saying that they will look to improve in this game.

India (Playing XI) - Ishan Kishan, Rishabh Pant (WK), Suryakumar Yadav, Shreyas Iyer, Hardik Pandya (C), Deepak Hooda, Harshal Patel (In for Washington Sundar), Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj, Yuzvendra Chahal.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Devon Conway (WK), Mark Chapman (In for Kane Williamson), Glenn Phillips, Daryl Mitchell, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi, Tim Southee (C), Adam Milne, Lockie Ferguson.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Anjum Chopra and Ajay Jadeja are pitch side. The pitch was covered for almost two hours. There is a bit of grass on the surface but it is hard underneath. There is not too much moisture and the square boundaries are a bit small as well. The ball will grip a bit and the captain winning the toss would like to bowl first. The bowlers will need to be spot-on with their lengths and batting second should be a good decision.

UPDATE 11.54 am IST (6.24 am GMT) - Good news for all cricket fans as the covers are completely off and the toss will take place very shortly, at 12 pm IST (6.30 am GMT). The play is scheduled to begin at 12.30 pm IST (7 am GMT) if there is no further rain. Stick around for the toss and team updates.

UPDATE 11.44 AM IST (6.14 AM GMT) - There is a loud cheer from the crowd as a bit of sunshine makes it way onto the ground. The rain has settled into a slight drizzle at the moment and apart from the main pitch, the covers have been taken off. Stay tuned for more updates.

UPDATE 11.25 AM IST (5.55 AM GMT) -There has been rain around Napier almost the whole of the day but the good news, for now, is that the rain has almost gone away completely. The outfield is still wet and the main pitch remains under covers. There is going to be a delay as the Toss has been officially delayed but hopefully, we will get a complete game. Stick around for further updates.

For India, there was a new captain, a new playing XI, and complete dominance against the regular NZ T20I side. It couldn't have gotten any better than this for Hardik Pandya while Suryakumar Yadav continued his scintillating form. In the bowling department, Washington Sundar broke a crucial partnership, Chahal and Siraj bagged two wickets each whilst Deepak Hooda went on to finish with bowling figures of 4 for 10 from 2.5 Overs. India will be hoping for a similar performance in this game as well. Can they win this series 2-0? Or will the hosts bounce back and level the series? Let's find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

The Kiwis aren't used to getting such thrashing at home. Kane Williamson was the top scorer for the hosts with a 61 off 52-ball knock which never made any impact but he is set to miss this game due to medical reasons. Considering the skipper’s form of late, it is bad news for the Blackcaps if Williamson is the top team batsman in a T20I match. New Zealand are a strong team and they know how to bounce back. They have done it before. Finn Allen, Devon Conway, and Glenn Phillips can be the game changers for New Zealand. They will look to improve their bowling in this game and avoid the mistakes made in their previous game.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage from McLean Park, Napier as India takes on New Zealand in the final game of the T20I series. The hosts will look for revenge after the thrashing received in the 2nd T20I at Mount Maunganui. It wasn’t an easy pitch to bat on but Suryakumar Yadav showed why he is so highly rated. India will be looking to win the series now whilst the hosts will look to bounce back and level the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The fleeting pace at which enthralling action comes our way keeps us the cricketing enthusiasts on the edge of our seats. After a short turnaround, we have arrived at the third and final T20I in India’s tour of New Zealand to be played at McLean Park in Napier. The visitors go into this game with a 1-0 lead having won the second T20I by a comfortable margin of 65 runs. The first game at Wellington was abandoned due to rain and both teams needed to win the previous match as India now enter the series decider knowing that they will not lose the series here. The Kiwis will be eager to secure a win and level the series, especially after the disappointment they experienced in the World Cup. In the last match, the hosts won the toss and elected to bowl first but were unable to restrict India to a low score. The opening bowlers could not get early breakthroughs and they conceded 72 runs in the last five overs to allow the game to slip away from them. Lockie Ferguson picked up two wickets and Ish Sodhi chipped in with one but their best bowling performance came from Tim Southee who bowled an outstanding last over claiming a Hat-trick and conceding just 5 runs. His effort prevented the visitors from crossing the 200-run mark but the run chase seemed difficult nonetheless. Devon Conway and Kane Williamson were the only two batters who looked comfortable at the wicket with the former getting dismissed after getting off to a start but the skipper went on to score a half-century. His strike rate is a major worry though as he gets off to a slow start which builds pressure on the other batters to score at a brisk rate. The middle and lower order crumbled and New Zealand were bowled out with 7 balls to spare. Mohammed Siraj and Yuzvendra Chahal claimed two wickets while Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Washington Sundar took one wicket each but the pick of the bowlers was Deepak Hooda who claimed four wickets with his part-time spin and conceded just 10 runs. All the plaudits for the comprehensive win will go to the Player of the Match Suryakumar Yadav who scored a swashbuckling century to register his second T20I ton. Ishan Kishan scored a handy cameo opening the innings but the majority of the runs came from the bat of the number one T20I batter in the world. India’s gamble to play Rishabh Pant as an opener did not pay off and they may decide to go with an established opener in form of Shubman Gill. Shreyas Iyer will hope to come good with the bat soon as there is ample competition for a spot in the starting XI with Sanju Samson waiting on the sidelines. With a series win on the line, VVS Laxman and Hardik Pandya may not opt to shuffle the pack much and stick to the winning eleven. New Zealand on the other hand, are missing Trent Boult at the start of the inning and will be hoping Adam Milne can fill the massive boots of the left-arm pacer. Lockie Ferguson was far too expensive and the rest of the bowlers seemed to lack penetration. Finn Allen needs a big inning under his belt while the form of Daryl Mitchell and James Neesham seems to be slightly worrisome. The forecast for Tuesday is not pleasant as there are showers expected and all we can do is keep our fingers crossed that rain stays away. Will India remain unbeaten and clinch a series win? Will New Zealand level the series and share the spoils? Or will it be the rain gods that triumph and not lets us have a result? We will find out soon.
